rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites wrongly think their misconduct will stay hidden; God can expose them so people recognize them and are not deceived.
rows.anchor: Time has now come that they be exposed so that everyone fully recognizes them and no one is deceived by them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart's malady includes hypocrisy and resentment toward Islam and Muslims; jealousy and malice intensify the hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: refers both to hypocrisy and to malice and jealousy which these hypocrites had for Islam and the Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term daghan is plural of daghn and means malice.
rows.anchor: The word ﺿْﻐﺎن  is a plural of ﺿﻐْﻦٌ  and means “malice.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lahn means tawriyah: a speaker privately intends one connotation while communicating a different meaning.
rows.anchor: also means tawriyah ie a person states something in a manner that it has a specific connotation in his heart yet he communicates a different meaning to others.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites practiced equivocal speech to make both Muslims and disbelievers believe their sympathies lay with them.
rows.anchor: They would converse in a dubious manner so as to convince both Muslims and the disbelievers at the same time

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could expose hypocrites through distinctive marks for the Prophet to recognize; concealing them is divine generosity, not inability.
rows.anchor: it is not at all difficult for God to expose them so that the Prophet (sws) is able to recognize them by their distinctive marks

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet can identify them from double-meaning words, hesitant speech, and dubious conversation.
rows.anchor: He can easily recognize them through their double-meaning words, hesitant talk and dubious conversation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deceiving Muslims with ambiguous words is no achievement because God knows their deeds, so hiding them from people gains nothing.
rows.anchor: if they are able to deceive Muslims through their dual and dubious words, then this is no success they should be proud of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tests people through good and bad circumstances to sift out those who truly strive and persevere from mere claimants.
rows.anchor: the Almighty will necessarily test and try them through good and bad circumstances of various types

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trials aim to identify fighters for God's cause and the persevering; as a consequence, deceptive pretenders to Muslim identity are exposed.
rows.anchor: the real purpose of these trials is to pinpoint the fighters for the cause of God and those who persevere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word akhbar refers to people's circumstances; testing sorts the good and consequently identifies evildoers.
rows.anchor: refers to their circumstances. This, in other words, can be understood that God tests people to sift out the good among them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic lām stresses that testing is a necessary part of God's established practice.
rows.anchor: Since this trial is a requisite of God’s established practice, it has been mentioned in an emphatic way by employing the assertive particle lām.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here, ʿalima means to sift out and discern.
rows.anchor: here means to sift out and to discern, as explained at an appropriate place in this exegesis.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's closing passage returns to its opening subject and warns hypocrites that disbelievers' opposition to God and His Messenger will fail and ruin the opponents in both lives.
rows.anchor: at the end, the sūrah turns to the same topic with which it began

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers intended here are Quraysh and their allies; verse one describes them with the same wording.
rows.anchor: show that the Quraysh and their allies are implied here as the disbelievers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents know the Messenger's call is true, yet resist out of pride in their leadership; this opposition cannot harm God's religion and will end in their humiliation.
rows.anchor: merely in conceit of their leadership

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though addressed generally, the command especially targets the weak Muslims just discussed; obedience to God and the Messenger must be complete and above vested interests in every circumstance.
rows.anchor: it is specially directed towards weak Muslims who are under discussion in the previous verses

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience makes deeds fruitful; subordinating it to self-interest can nullify even religious acts, since God accepts faith according to His terms.
rows.anchor: through this obedience only their deeds will bear fruit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will not forgive those who disbelieve, obstruct others from His path, and die persisting in disbelief.
rows.anchor: stopped others from treading the path leading to God and then died while remaining adamant on this disbelief

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who seek the disbelievers' support and conspire to preserve their friendship face the same fate.
rows.anchor: the same fate will be met by people who will seek their support and conspire to keep their friendship intact with them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salm means peace and reconciliation; the hypocrites, lacking courage to fight, kept advocating peace, as in the earlier discussion of verses 22–23.
rows.anchor: since these hypocrites do not have the courage to fight, they would keeping talking about peace and reconciliation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites' peace policy arose from cowardice and self-interest disguised as amity; the verse exposes this and calls them to wage jihad with faith and courage, promising God's help and full recompense.
rows.anchor: founded on their cowardice and vested interests; but they would call people to it in the garb of peace and amity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax resembles 2:42: when both parts of a coordinated clause express one reality, the negative particle need not be repeated.
rows.anchor: when both parts of a conjugate clause express the same reality.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted negative particle makes clear that the call for peace stems from cowardice rather than love of peace.
rows.anchor: this call to peace is not because they are peace-loving but because this is an unsuccessful attempt to hide their cowardice

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression wa tarahu haqqahu means that a person was dishonest regarding another person's rights.
rows.anchor: he was dishonest in the rights of a person

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should not fear God will shortchange them in recompense; He will fully reward every deed, so there is no reason to avoid sacrifice.
rows.anchor: God will be insincere or untruthful to them regarding the reward of their deeds; on the contrary, He will richly reward them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly resources matter only when used to earn the Hereafter; a life spent enslaved to desire is meaningless, while faith, virtue, and spending bring God's rich reward and an eternal kingdom.
rows.anchor: the wealth and resources of this life have any value, then it is only this much that a person uses them to earn for the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about God not asking for all wealth suppresses ḥafāʾ, as the next verse clarifies; Qur'anic brevity often lets the answer explain a concise question.
rows.anchor: Briefly stating something before explaining it is a common style of the Qur’ ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥafāʾ means taking something completely or demanding it insistently.
rows.anchor: to take something completely and totally or to demand something insistently.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording reassures the fainthearted that God will ask for only part of their wealth and richly recompense them, so they should not fear spending or resent the call.
rows.anchor: He will only demand a part of it and in this too He will richly recompense them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Demanding all or most of their wealth would expose the hypocrites' stinginess and hidden malice and jealousy; God's restraint is a favor for which they should be grateful.
rows.anchor: He does not do so for this would expose people whose stinginess and hypocrisy are as yet under cover.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This restates the warning at verse 29 that hypocrites should not assume God will conceal their malice and jealousy forever.
rows.anchor: they should not be deceived by the fact that the Almighty will conceal their malice and jealousy forever.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author treats hypocrites' stinginess as a refusal that amounts to apostasy and warns they can be replaced.
rows.anchor: sound a threat to the hypocrites that their attitude is akin to apostasy.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks them to spend for their own benefit, so He can reward them with the eternal kingdom.
rows.anchor: Himself but for themselves so that He can reward them the eternal kingdom in recompense.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi links the threat of replacement to 5:54, where God replaces apostates with people who love Him and are loved by Him.
rows.anchor: similar words used for hypocrites are:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The replacements love God and seek His pleasure, unlike hypocrites who harbor malice toward God and earn His revulsion.
rows.anchor: these hypocrites harbour malice for God and have absolutely no interest in earning the pleasure of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites seek friendship with disbelievers and are exploited against Islam; their replacements will be gracious to believers and resist disbelievers like a solid wall.
rows.anchor: they will find the believers to be like a rock solid wall
